name: High-vol Bollinger-floor reversion (volatility-overshoot snap)
rationale: THESIS: a lower-Bollinger-band touch only mean-reverts when vol is HIGH — in high-vol regimes the bands are wide and a deep negative z-score is a genuine overshoot driven by forced selling that snaps back; in calm regimes the bands are tight and a band touch is just a slow drift lower that keeps going. We buy when Bollinger z-score is below a fitted floor (bb_z BOUNDED) ARMED by realized vol above a fitted high-vol floor (vol_realized BOUNDED). DISCONFIRMER: run the IDENTICAL bb_z<floor rule with the vol_realized>floor gate REMOVED (bare band-touch buy). If high-vol-armed is not materially better risk-adjusted net of fees, the vol regime adds nothing and this is plain band-touch dip-buying. Cross-check: LOW-vol-armed version of the same rule should underperform.
catalyst: Price pierces the lower Bollinger band (deep negative z-score) while realized vol is elevated — a wide-band overshoot in a panic tape.
